name: charts.mapsset2.pic057.ideas-in-biology-that-resulted-from-the-ideonomy-project
of: idea in biology that resulted from the Ideonomy Project
items: All life (the bios) as one great self-contagion.
Anosogens; displacive and cancellative counter-contagions and counter-diseases; finite, quantic, and saturable 'pathogenic niches'; noncontagious and non-nucleic anosogens.
Captured contagions; organelles (such as mitochondria) as captured ancient contagions.

Constant evolution, reconstruction, and/or restabilization of the bios via "lateral gene flows" (or informational contagions) ascending from the tiniest-scale organisms up to the biggest organisms and biological phenomena.

Constant evolution, reevolution, and/or redifferentiation of the bios via "lateral gene flows" (or informational contagions) descending from the greatest spatiotemporal scales and organisms down to the least.

Constant inter-evolution and intercoordination of the bios (all life) via countercurrent "lateral gene flows" (or informational contagions) ascending and descending between the least and greatest biological scales and organisms and reversing at the antipolar extremes.
Creation and release of artificial 'sosogens, anosogens, and antinosogens' by future medical, agricultural, and ecological technology.
Cutaneous, oral, and intestinal microflora as 'sosogens' (good diseases).
Danger that future medical extirpation of diseases will simultaneously extirpate 'proseases' that are necessary to health.
Diseases as grossly misunderstood phenomena that are really normal, beneficial, and even necessary to all life.
Diseases peculiar to single cells (cytodiseases and cytopathology).

Do the bodily microflorae of the world's people, or of all creatures, migrate slowly but inexorably everywhere, as a vast blanket-like pandemic that is a paradoxically indissociable continuum of 'good and bad diseases'?
Epidemic diseases as microorganismal migrations (nature's fastest and most massive migrations).
Improving the 'sosology' of bowel 'proseases' to reduce digestive system diseases and discomforts.
Lineal evolution as but an internalized by-product of predominant 'lateral evolution', or 'lateral gene flows', and quasi-autonomous, self-maintaining equilibria in such flows.
Micro-contagions between and within the body's elements, as the smallest epidemiological scale.
Representing information under pressure exploding from level to level or metamorphosing into endless new forms and manifestations.
Redesigned or artificial digestive microflora enabling men and agricultural animals to synthesize their own vitamins.
Single 'laterally flowing genes' as the tiniest contagions.
Sympathogens (pathogens that can or must act in concert with other pathogens to produce, amplify, or transform a disease or epidemic).

name: charts.mapsset2.pic058.8-other-ideas-in-biology-that-resulted-from-ideonomy-project
of: idea in biology that resulted from Ideonomy Project
items: Analogs of animal territoriality throughout biology (e.g., private, organized, and competitive domains, and domainal behavior, of plants, bacteria, organs, cells (such as neurons), biomolecules, and genes).

Analogs of plant allelopathy and 'allelophily' throughout biology (e.g., in animals or protists, intra-organismally between or within organs, cells (such as neurons), organelles, or biomolecules, or in evolution or ontogeny).
Asthma as due to mechanisms evolved by plants to repel groups of animals from their territories.
Autopathy and autophily (or self-allelopathy and self-'allelophily'), as a relaxed or reflexive analog and counter-analog of allelopathy.

Geochemical differences among soils, and even some ore deposits, as caused by cumulative sequestration of chemical elements and species by plants over their ranges in the course of geological time—e.g., for their own nutrition, for evolving certain soil textures, as a result of long-range mass-allelopathy or mass-'allelophily', to 'toxically repel' unwanted animals (pests) from their territories gradually over countless generations, etc.
Nonstandard 'pecking orders' and evolutionary analogs of pecking orders in animals (e.g., 'pecking circles', variable and multidimensional 'pecking orders', etc).
'Pecking order' analogs in plants and microbes.
Plant allelophily (as a counter-analog of allelopathy).

name: charts.mapsset2.pic173.why-microbes-may-be-higher-forms-of-life-than-macroorganisms
of: reason why microbes may be higher forms of life than macroorganisms
items: Far OLDER, and hence have had longer to evolve and become 'perfect'.
Far MORE NUMEROUS: contemporary global population perhaps 10 exp 28-30 microbionts.

SHORTEST-LIVED [with life-spans as short as perhaps 20 minutes; may even spend almost all of their existence procreating; total generations in history of earth may have been vastly greater than for larger organisms, producing 10 exp ~42 microbionts], HENCE may have far GREATER OPPORTUNITY TO EVOLVE, adapt, become perfect or self-integrated; diversify, complicate, and differentiate, seize and retain power, experiment and learn empirically, become Gaians, etc.
In terms of #3: may be PROTEAN, the BIOS's PERPETUALLY varying, ADAPTIVE, exploratory, AND EXPERIMENTAL FLOOR that 'looks at all possibilities of things'.

May represent a far GREATER RANGE OF SPECIES, subspecies, or biontic or merely potential polymorphisms, or EVEN A VARIATIONAL CONTINUUM more fundamental than species or other discrete taxa; may comprise a much larger range of phenes, genes, co-phenes (polygenic phenes), co-genes (pleiotropic genes), monogenic phenes and monophenic genes (genotypal and phenotypal specialization), and 'nonstandard' genetic, quasi-genetic, and sexual mechanisms.
May be far LESS STABLE and hence far more variable, or far MORE unstable or metastable, and hence ABLE TO LEARN AND SENSITIVE TO CONDITIONS.
May be far MORE STABLE--life at its most enduring and durable.
Far MORE UNIVERSAL--ubiquitous over the earth and within its multifold environments and conditions--and hence possessed of a far greater range of experience and worldly wisdom.

May be the great biological MEMORY used and reembody all larger--or all other--organisms; a storehouse or library into which experiences or summaries of experiences, masses of special and/or general problems, solutions, situational parameters and values, mathematical series and formulas, canonical forms, behavioral, morphogenetic, ontogenetic, and evolutionary routines and algorithms, tactics, strategies, body-plans, ecological groups' (groups in the mathematical sense), etc] are put, where they may lie passive, remain active, or live a perpetually interactive and crypto-evolutionary existence, or continue to play some subtle, indirect, and undiscovered large-scale evolutionary role.

Perhaps being FREE TO TRAVEL ENDLESSLY WITHIN AND BETWEEN ALL OTHER ORGANISMS, may have had--and continue to have--opportunity to know, explore, and master all those organisms or the bios in its integral totality.

Most--possibly all--LARGER ORGANISMS [directly or indirectly] may be absolutely DEPENDENT upon [in a trophic, environment-transforming, and cosmopoietic sense], whereas the microbes, in general, may be absolutely independent and autonomous.

Microbes--or their suborganisms ['meronts': viruses, viroids, etc]--may function, or have evolved, as carriers of genetic information back and forth between all other--or all--taxa; and in their messenger, mediative capacity--AS THE AGENTS or coagents OF HORIZONTAL GENE FLOW--may have achieved a unique centrality that led to supreme--possibly Gaian--CONTROL OVER THE BIOS, in either a partial or a comprehensive sense.

On--or CLOSEST TO--the actual length, time, mass, energy, etc SCALES OF BIOCHEMICAL PROCESSES, structures, and units: microbes may naturally have acquired the greatest and most fundamental molecular and physiological sophistication, and may represent the 'consultative plane' of biochemical innovation and interadjustment for all of the larger organisms.
May have an ASYMMETRIC PATHOGENIC POWER to devastate or extinguish all larger life, while remaining sublimely invulnerable to the latter.

Being CLOSEST TO THE GENETIC, suborganismal, and micro-phenic LEVEL [cf. #12]: may permit or involve the fastest lineal or cross-lineal transfers and interchanges of genetic information, innovations, adaptations, commands, messages, etc.

On--or CLOSEST TO--the actual length, time, mass, energy, etc SCALES OF BIOCHEMICAL PROCESSES, structures, and units: microbes may naturally have acquired the greatest and most fundamental molecular and physiological sophistication, and may represent the 'consultative plane' of biochemical innovation and interadjustment for all or the larger organisms.
14. May have an ASYMMETRIC PATHOGENIC POWER to devastate or extinguish all larger life, while remaining sublimely invulnerable to the latter.

15. Being CLOSEST TO THE GENETIC, suborganismal, and micro-phenic LEVEL [cf. #12]: may permit or involve the fastest lineal or cross-lineal transfers and interchanges of genetic information, innovations, adaptations, commands, messages, etc.

16. May represent the LEAST SPECIALIZED AND/OR THE MOST GENERALIZED FORM OF LIFE, or the most generalized, primitive, fundamental, persistent, all-important, or all-directive biological (bios) information or universal evolutionary plan; by contrast, larger organisms--and in proportion to their largeness or (supposed) 'level of advancement'--may be excessively or even aberrantly specialized or 'noisy' (dissonant).

17. [BODILY SYSTEMS, organs, tissues, cell types, organelles, biochemical pathways and mechanisms, hormones, large-scale bodily functions, various mechanical, electrical, and chemical devices, sensors, effectors, etc] that are seen IN LARGER ORGANISMS may simply be larger-scale, explicit, specialized, or simplified isomorphic, homomorphic, polygenous, or polymorphic RE-CREATIONS (projections, so to say) OF CONSTANT OR ARCHETYPAL INNOVATIONS BY microbes on the microscopic or ultramicroscopic scale; microbes may SYNTHESIZE AND EMBODY--in REALIZED OR LATENT [unrecognizable, schematic, virtual, or 'ideonomical'] form--whole classes, or a veritable hierarchy or network of taxa of CLASSES, OF such currently or perhaps one day useful INVENTIONS.

18. GENOMES OF all LARGER ORGANISMS may be DYNAMICALLY UNSTABLE over the long term, AND DERIVE such STABILITY as they have FROM periodic or incessant adjustments by or acquisitions or interchanges of genes from or via microbes and/or suborganisms, either because the latter represent by far the larger or combinatorially most various 'gene pool' or because the latter mediate the horizontal gene flow and dynamic unity of the one and irreducible genotype and phenotype that all life on earth--the spatiotemporally indivisible bios--really represents; and conceivably all LARGER--or all--ORGANISMS are 'CONTINUALLY REEVOLVING' FROM the smaller or smallest.

19. Even in a general way [cf. #18], it is NOT CLEAR that MACROORGANISMS should be treated as INDEPENDENT ORGANISMS, or as DIVISIBLE FROM the microbes that may be their multifold symbiotic partners, 'external or shared organelles', or whatever.

20. May be the MOST EFFICIENT organisms in one-or many ways: the acquisition, storage, transmission, use, or transformation of any form or forms of energy, matter, space, etc [incl. the extraction, processing, movement, etc of geochemicals]; locomotion or cellular movement; intracellular operations, biochemical syntheses, transformation or regulation of the external environment; transmission, processing, or storage of various forms of biological information; reproduction or sexuality; [miniaturization, acceleration, combination, multiplexing, modulation, alternation, specialization, standardization, systematization, stabilization, control, stratification, etc] of functions; achievement of redundancy or irredundancy; etc.

21. May be the HEART OF GAIA: in the sense of being that which originated and now maintains, protects, directs, and/or evolves the life-favorable elements and phenomena of the geos [geological, hydrological, and atmospheric].

22. LIFE may mainly or simultaneously be EVOLVING BACKWARDS TOWARD SIMPLICITY OR THE TINIEST forms of matter, or may be predominantly evolving around the eschatological and archological 'black hole' or 'essential singularity' of the genome or chromosomes.

23. FOR BEING THE SIMPLEST organisms or the organisms with the fewest parts or least cumbersome and interfering genomes [or, more esoterically, for being that which is closest to the paradoxically and mysteriously preinfinite and supertemporal apeiron]: MAY BE THE MOST EVOLVED, in general or in special and key ways.
24. May actually have EVOLVED LARGER ORGANISMS: to serve as useful servants, vehicles, tools, habitats, or experiments.

25. It is NOT NECESSARILY true that the smallest organisms--or at least, neontological forms of same--are the MOST ANCIENT or least derivative; larger organisms, or what we call higher organisms, may have come earlier and given rise to at least those tiniest organisms we see around us today, or the latter may be utterly transformed versions or mimics of what were in fact the earliest, most primitive, lowest, or tiniest organisms.

26. 'LARGENESS' OR MULTICELLULARITY--against the near-infinity of other and orthogonal biological dimensions--may be a relatively superficial and even IRRELEVANT trait that is merely conspicuous or anthropocentric; the presently or ultimately most advanced or important evolutionary directions, vectors, or goals may be unrelated, dimensionless, merely additive, or synthetic and even 'holonomical': with respect to size, mass, redundancy (meristic or auxetic), complexity, longevity, or the like.
27. SIMILARLY [vide #26] FOR OTHER ANTHROPOMORPHOUS DIMENSIONS and qualities: not excepting even intelligence or civilization [at least as we ourselves know or are conscious of them].
28. Evolution's thrust and accomplishment may essentially be bipolar and antisyzygial: with LIFE AT ITS SMALLEST as important as, and complementary or even COESSENTIAL TO, LIFE AT ITS BIGGEST.

34. We already know of MANY WAYS [anatomical, physiological, etc] in which microbes are definitely much MORE ADVANCED than--or excel--larger and so-called 'higher' organisms.

35. Some novel and clearly REVOLUTIONARY BIOLOGICAL SYSTEMS and phenomena MAY EXIST IN microbes that evidently have yet to be independently evolved in, or transferred to, larger and supposedly higher--or highest--organisms.

36. name: charts.mapsset2.pic179.alternative-meanings-and-implications-of-the-gaia-hypothesis
of: alternative meaning or implication of the 'Gaia Hypothesis'
items: 1. The BIOS CURRENTLY exercises greater—perhaps much greater—CONTROL over earth's GEOS: its GEOSPHERE [its geochemistry and even geomorphology or geophysics], ATMOSPHERE [atmospheric composition, structure, and dynamics—incl. climate], and/or HYDROSPHERE than per the orthodox view.

2. The bios FORMERLY, has ALWAYS, or ORIGINALLY played a greater—perhaps much greater—role in CREATING, TRANSFORMING, REGULATING, MAINTAINING, and/or RETRANSFORMING the geos than tradition ever imagined or contemporary earth scientists believe.

3. The bios plays or has played, IF NOT necessarily A GREATER THAN A [broader, more diverse, stranger, more complex, more direct or indirect, more multilevel, more sustained, more capable or 'adaptive', more stabilizing, destabilizing, or evolutionary, more primary, important, or critical, more interactive, complementary, or supplementary, more generalized or specialized, different, and/or as yet unknown or even unimagined] role in the earth sciences than has been assumed.

4. The BIOS AS A WHOLE, OR MERELY some limited PART OF IT [in terms of size of organism, species, taxonomic level, community, or biome; or in terms of some subsystem within an organism or set of organisms], may alternatively have played, or play, these Gaian roles.
5. Alternatively, EXTRABIOLOGICAL NATURE—earth's geology, climate, or ocean—may play or have played the postulated Gaian roles, either essentially alone or in cooperation with the bios.

6. Life's Gaian control over the economy and destiny of earth may have taken a DEMOCRATIC form, essentially being exerted upwards as the [holistic or cumulative] effect of the collective actions, experiences, laws, interactions, and/or associations of all, or else of a majority or plurality of bionts.

7. Alternatively, life's Gaian control over the economy and destiny of earth may have taken a CENTRALIZED form, essentially being exerted downward from above—as the expression of a relatively simple over-governing agency or set of rules, patterns, trends, possibilities, coordinations, and/or the like.

8. Regardless of whether life's Gaian control of the earth has had a mainly descending ('centralized') or ascending ('democratic') form, the character thereof may have been either INDIVIDUALISTIC or TOTALITARIAN.
9. Life's role as Gaia may have been or be a compromise or MIXTURE of any or all OF THESE—or of seemingly opposite and antagonistic—POSSIBILITIES.
10. One or just a few key COMPONENTS of earth's bios, geology, climate, and/or ocean may enjoy a surprisingly 'Gaian' stability, adaptiveness, flexibility, or autonomy.

11. The internal structure or processes of life may—as a result either of natural selection or chance—TOLERATE far GREATER EXTREMES or ranges of possibilities—whether biogenic, cosmogenic, or anthropogenic—than conventionally assumed.
12. The bios, or some of its critical components, may be capable of far FASTER, MORE EFFICIENT, more comprehensive, and/or deeper EVOLUTION, ADJUSTMENT, or responses than hitherto supposed.

13. The bios may include similarly efficient, powerful, and unsuspected mechanisms for the MUTUAL ADJUSTMENT, adaptation, simultaneous transformation, mutual ASSISTANCE, synergistic behavior, and/or biogeographic redisposition of the totality OF its BIONTS, species, and/or systems.

14. The naturally selected and evolved behavior, structure, and constitution of separate bionts, species, and higher TAXA may be much more 'ALTRUISTIC', 'societal', interdetermined, collaborative, PLANFUL, PRESCIENT, prevenient, and 'TRANSCENDENTAL' (of space and even time) than orthodoxy holds.
15. The organelles, genes, molecules, systems, organs, 'orders', and/or even 'purposes' of different ORGANISMS may be far more COEVOLVED, MUTUALLY DERIVED, and/or interfluent than believed.
16. The effects of PHYSICAL PROCESSES or events upon life—or simply upon inanimate nature—may be MEDIATED, modified, and transformed BY LIFE in an unexpectedly major or thoroughgoing way.

17. LIFE may play a significant, minimal, or critical ROLE in some of the most ordinary or unexpected major or minor GEOLOGICAL, ATMOSPHERIC, or OCEANIC PROCESSES: e.g. clouds, precipitation, atmospheric cycles, the reflectivity, transmissivity, and heat capacity of the atmosphere, sea ice, cryoconite holes, the expansion and contraction of deserts, marine transgression and regression, earth mounds, the ice caps, deep soil, crystallogenesis, groundwater at considerable depth, and even things as fantastically improbable as earthquakes, volcanoes, continental drift, orogeny, rock metamorphosis, the formation of mineral deposits deep in the earth, the escape of water and gas from deep in the earth, or continent formation.

18. There may be BIOLOGICAL PHENOMENA—and controls—that characteristically exist and operate AT a much HIGHER level IN SPACE, in TIME, or on other 'natural HIERARCHIES' than is apparent to us at present.

19. Should the entire bios constitute a single immense organism, the evolutionary or 'biological' level represented by such a SUPERORGANISM may be ANALOGOUS TO anything from that of a virus, bacterium, fungus, alga, nematode, —or parasite—, to the 'level' (or modus) of a plant, sponge, insect, fish, mammal, man (human intelligence), or superman; then again, it may be something utterly sui generis.

20. MUCH of what is PERCEIVED AS as being unhealthy, PATHOLOGICAL, DESTRUCTIVE, catastrophic, or otherwise unfortunate, flawed, wrong, or merely ACCIDENTAL in biological nature—including the existence of organisms usually described as being "pathogenic", "parasitic", or just "curiously" anomalous—may in reality be altogether benign, BENEFICIAL, or necessary in some as yet undetected Gaian scheme or process.

name: charts.mapsset2.pic180.alternative-bases-for-major-theories-of-evolution
of: alternative basis for a major theory of evolution
items: Direct adaptation by inheritance of results of use or disuse of organs: LAMARCKIAN EVOLUTION.

Evolution based on some principle or animus 'seeking' PERFECTION: which may variously mean a mere reduction of errors, an increase of regularity, probability, or reliability, an interderivation of forms, a maximal simplification of production, or myriad other things.

ANTICIPATORY EVOLUTION: some form or degree however limited, exceptional, or subtle, and however slow, multigenerational, or indirect of purposeful or foresightful adaptation, improvisation, or innovation on the species, biontic, or bios level; per contra the usual assumption, this need not involve volition, perception, or intelligence on any of the levels—at least not in the usual sense. For example, through natural selection operating on the bios level, the bios may have acquired some instinctive model, abstract dynamical simulation, lawful knowledge, logical, behavioral, or meta-behavioral repertoire, computational or strategic facility, or N-dimensional representation of arbitrarily high dimensionality of—or for dealing with—the biological environment or real-world phenomena or series thereof, some enormously or peculiarly generalized image of reality or way of operating, that confers upon evolution a modest but surprising anticipatory aspect. The possibilities under this heading greatly transcend what Theodosius Dobzhansky referred to as "autogenesis", the unfolding of the potentialities hidden in the organism, impelled by an urge toward development in a certain direction. Teleonomical behavior is one possible expression of anticipatory evolution.
Evolution via Darwin's principle of natural SELECTION OF THE FITTEST variants produced by the interactions of genomes with organisms' external and internal environments.
Evolution via CATACLYSMIC UPHEAVAL: e.g. à la Richard Goldschmidt.

Evolution via BIOGENIC DISRUPTION: such disruption may alternatively or simultaneously be: on the organismic sub-organismal, biontic, species, ecosystem, or bios level; ultimately or partly extrabiological or instead exclusively biogenic; stochastic or rigidly deterministic; cyclical, aperiodic, a response to situational need or opportunity, or the result of some more complex form of managerial readiness; uniform or multiform; limited or catastrophic; temporary or continuous; episodic or progressive; genotypal or phenotypal (so to say); optimal or crude; experimental or merely performative; overt or covert; etc.
EVOLUTION DETERMINED BY THE WHOLE FORM OF THE BIOS (i.e., holistically on the bios level)—or instead on the sub-bios level of individual species, populations, or bionts.

TOLERANCE by some ['fitness' and/or 'autogenetic'] mechanism of random and/or lawful [exogenous and/or endogenous] differentiation that [minimally, optimally, or maximally] [exhausts or 'saturates'] [phenotypal and/or genotypal] possibilities.
COENABLEMENT by different forms being evolved, of different forms.

"NOMOGENESIS": in the NOVEL sense of the progressive, directive evolution of preferential laws of further evolution or of a progressive hierarchy of self-regulatory processes—and possibly of ever-higher meta-laws of laws....

VERGENT EQUIVALENCE: the coalescent cooperation of divergent and convergent processes in the progressive production of ever-higher-order multidimensional equivalences of phenes, phenotypes, and taxa—and/or, perhaps the progressive mutual integration of all of the latter.
EVOLUTION CONTROLLED BY VAST or infinite PHENES or HEREDITARY FACTORS, 'vast' qua vastly more numerous and/or diverse than per the orthodox picture.

items: 11. 'NOMOGENESIS': in the NOVEL sense of the progressive, directive evolution of preferential laws of further evolution or of a progressive hierarchy of self-regulatory processes—and possibly of ever-higher meta-laws of laws....

12. VERGENT EQUIVALENCE: the coalescent cooperation of divergent and convergent processes in the progressive production of ever-higher-order multidimensional equivalences of phenes, phenotypes, and taxa—and/or, perhaps the progressive mutual integration of all of the latter.
13. EVOLUTION CONTROLLED BY VAST or infinite PHENES or HEREDITARY FACTORS; 'vast' qua vastly more numerous and/or diverse than per the orthodox picture.

14. HOLONOMICAL EVOLUTION: sensu a 'mysterious', infinitely simple or infinitely complex direction of evolutionary processes by some holistic, unitary factor or factors transcending space—and perhaps transcending time as well.
16. INFINITE (transtemporal or supratemporal) COMPLEXITY. Apropos, there is some reason to believe that 'infinite complexity' preexists in physical nature—ergo in all of nature and all science.
20. ALEATORY EVOLUTION: biogenic or extrabiological chance playing a major, a coequal and interactive, or the dominant role in evolution.

21. ORTHOGENESIS: sensu evolution toward a single goal or—far less or more restrictively—along a single path, direction, axis, or vector (whether rectilinear, curvilinear, 2-cylindrical, 3-cylindrical, conical, triangular, or whatever).
22. MONOTHEMATIC EVOLUTION: sensu constant variations upon approximately a single theme.

23. 'COMBINATORIAL' EVOLUTION: evolution involving and via ever broader, pyramidal exploitation of previously evolved or encountered phenes—through their progressive intercombination, autocombination (á la autocorrelation), permutation (self-permutation and inter-permutation), and/or transformation.

24. CONSERVATIVE (stoichiometric) EVOLUTION: sensu evolution that more or less constantly conserves certain aboriginal, early, or emergent quantities (constants), phenes, equations, systems, meta-systems, relationships, laws, organs, and/or the like.
25. ITERATIVE EVOLUTION: evolution involving the constant reuse or repetition of certain presumably elementary operations.

27. HIERARCHICAL EVOLUTION: sensu the evolution of a hierarchy of levels (dependent, interdependent, or independent); (similar, adjoint, or dissimilar); (symmetric or asymmetric); (supersedural or coactive); or hierarchies thereof (themselves dependent, interdependent, or independent); etc.
30. 'CONVERGENT' EVOLUTION: in the NEOLOGISTIC SENSE of evolution tending toward a single final goal (a posteriori or a priori); of arbitrary complexity or simplicity.
31. ENTROPIC EVOLUTION—or instead NEGENTROPIC EVOLUTION: evolution that tends or seeks to increase or decrease entropy, or else that is governed by the or a increase or decrease of entropy.

32. RELAXATIONAL (even simplicity-'maximizing') EVOLUTION: sensu evolution that directly, eventually, or periodically seeks or tends to 'relax' into simpler states, processes, forms, or ways of doing things it has already evolved.

34. Per contra, EFFICIENCY-MAXIMIZING or efficiency-infinitizing EVOLUTION: evolution tending or seeking (inter alia or supremely) to push some or all types of efficiency to the all-out maximum or to infinity—say in the sense of doing as much as possible with as little as possible, in infinitely many or few ways, or with infinitesimal energy, matter, materials, space, experimentation, uncertainty, error, risk, cost, time, increase of entropy, motion, destruction, adjustment, repair, intermediate stages, or chaos.
35. EVOLUTION THAT SEEKS TO MAXIMIZE, infinitize, absolutize, or optimize—or instead, evolution that seeks to MINIMIZE one or more QUANTITIES, phenes, or 'traits of the bios proper'.

36. SPECIALIZED EVOLUTION—or instead GENERALIZING EVOLUTION: sensu evolution that to some extent, progressively, initially, or finally at once includes and excludes n-n features, dimensions, phenes, processes, domains, or other possibilities.

37. TERMINATING EVOLUTION—or instead SEMPITERNAL EVOLUTION: evolution with a minor or supreme tendency to draw to an absolute, partial, or periodic halt, or evolution that could or would go on forever.
38. ACCELERATING EVOLUTION—or instead DECELERATING EVOLUTION: whether arithmetic, exponential, hyperbolic, or whatever.
40. CONTINUOUS EVOLUTION—or instead DISCONTINUOUS EVOLUTION: uninterrupted evolution or interrupted or 'punctuated' evolution.

32. RELAXATIONAL (even simplicity-'maximizing') EVOLUTION: sensu evolution that directly, eventually, or periodically [seeks or tends] to 'relax' into simpler [states, processes, forms, or ways of doing things it has already evolved].

34. Per contra, [EFFICIENCY-MAXIMIZING or efficiency-infinitizing] EVOLUTION: evolution [tending or seeking (inter alia or supremely) to push some or all types of efficiency to the all-out maximum or to infinity—say in the sense of doing as much as possible with as little as possible, in infinitely many or few ways, or with infinitesimal energy, matter, materials, space, experimentation, uncertainty, error, risk, cost, time, increase of entropy, motion, destruction, adjustment, repair, intermediate stages, or chaos].

37. TERMINATING EVOLUTION—or instead SEMPITERNAL EVOLUTION [evolution with a minor or supreme tendency to draw to an absolute, partial, or periodic halt, or evolution that could or would go on forever].

40. CONTINUOUS EVOLUTION—or instead DISCONTINUOUS EVOLUTION [uninterrupted evolution or interrupted or 'punctuated' evolution].

41. RECAPITULATIVE EVOLUTION: in the special sense of evolution that [forever or pervasively] [seeks or tends] to evolve in [new or old] ways that [subtly or obviously] [resemble or represent] [new or old ways (evolutionary [sequences, processes, series, paths, or means)]. (This concept is not to be confused with palingenesis or with the simple recurrence of phenes).

42. RETROSPECTIVE EVOLUTION: the epistemological, seemingly metaphysical concept that evolution may be [or of evolution that is] of an exquisitely subjective nature in the sense that it can only be seen—definitely, clearly, or at all—in retrospect or from within, or being being a matter of so-called 'a posteriori order'.

43. [CHANGE-DIRECTED EVOLUTION—or instead STASIS-DIRECTED EVOLUTION: evolution that seeks to [increase or maximize] change, novelty, flow, transformation, motion, activity, dynamics, or the like, or in the second case, their opposites: equilibrium, stability, permanence, rigidity, immobility, statics, or whatever].

44. COALESCENT EVOLUTION: sensu a net or dominant tendency toward the [structural or functional] [coordination, intercoordination, pan-intercoordination, plexure, equilibration, concinnity, synergism, complementarity, interdependence, consilience, interlinkage, overlapping, integration, fusion, or identity; cooperation, mutual exploitation, standardization, synchronization, singularization, universalization, infinite ecology, mutual containment (concorporation), and/or the like] of all [species, taxa, taxonomic categories, bionts, generations, intra-organismal components, ecosystems, biomes, biotopes, or biospheric loci, instances, or phenomena].
